articleTitle: Surf's up: green construction industry
abstract: GREATER collaboration among architects, community planners, contractors, suppliers, and government regulators continues to bolster the widespread smart construction movement. Development of safer and sustainable structures has led to more use of local and ecologically friendly building materials. The trend today is to narrow adverse impacts on the built environment by internalizing costs, applying automation efficiently where most appropriate, conserving space requirements, promoting endurable influences, mitigating waste, and restraining consumption of natural resources. Websites described below are examples of the many online resources that address advantages, consequences, determinants, and components embodied in the greening of the construction industry.

articleTitle: Surf's up: Overcoming job stress
abstract: EVEN those of us who have had the good fortune to work for extended periods in an harmonious workplace have experienced occasional, often fortuitous, stressful episodes that are associated with our employment. Stressors in a work environment tend to be complex and often result from temporary errors in human judgment coupled with relentless behavior. Effects can be exacerbated by events such as high pressure assignments, business downsizing, outsourcing activities, mechanical or physical mishaps, unforeseen customer dissatisfaction, and changes in personal life situations. Personnel at all levels can be negatively affected by exposure to stressful situations. Productivity usually suffers when anxiety and tension exist among managers and coworkers. Websites abound that identify both professional mental health providers and avenues for self help. Below are examples of organizations and services that strive to provide guidance to companies and individuals for developing overall workplace contentment, composure, and trust.

articleTitle: Surf's up: harnessing information overload
abstract: Presents examples of resources that shed light on trends, tools, and solutions for addressing and overcoming huge amounts of wasted effort when confronted with too much information of dubious quality.

articleTitle: Social networking
abstract: IN this issue of EMR we look at the emergence of social networks that stem from modern communication tools. Driven by a need to share and collaborate, social networking is rapidly becoming a dominant way that we work with our colleagues, interact with our family, and conduct business transactions. The form that social networking tools and software have taken is not really what we expected when digital networks were designed and constructed. The speed that these tools have been adopted eclipses anything we've ever designed. Hardware design is increasingly driven by thinking about how a device will fit into existing social network systems.

articleTitle: The three faces of stress
abstract: In this article, the author summarizes the three faces of stress. The more we know about stress, the more control we will be able to have over our life. This knowledge is at the core of effective functioning.

articleTitle: Social networking? Bah! Humbug!
abstract: I DON'T KNOW about you, but I'm drowning in technology: from my computer, to my "smart" phone, to my iPad, to my television with all its "boxes", to my telephone calls to practically everyone I want to contact where I am greeted by another technology gadget: voice mail! I can't seem to get away from it all; it is everywhere!

articleTitle: Surf's up: social network services and analyses
abstract: SOCIAL network utilities have become worldwide phenomena that continue to attract scores of Internet enthusiasts. For example, there is the notion of the blogosphere, which is characterized by communal determination to share information and viewpoints. Weblogs are written as personal diaries that sometimes combine subjective thoughts with journalistic reporting. Capabilities of individual authors range from private novices to professional correspondents. Entries usually focus on specific topics and may contain hyperlinks to other relevant resources.

IEEE Technology Management Council
abstract: TMC publishes the IEEE Engineering Management Review, and the IEEE Transactions on Engineering Management. The Review, published since 1973, reprints from other publications significant articles and selected original materials related to professional practice. The Transactions, published since 1954, documents the original contributions that are being made to advance the theory and practice of engineering management. These publications, are provided to all TMC subscribers without additional charge. TMC also underwrites and sponsors conferences, educational products, books, and chapter activities of interest to its members.

Information overload
abstract: WHEN Alvin Toffler coined the term 'information overload' in his classic 1970 book, Future Shock, it is doubtful that even he imagined the formidable array of information sources that we now have access to. Speculation quickly surfaced that such an information supply could lead to poor decisions as the capacity of our human processing ability becomes taxed. Research has established that job productivity and performance can be severely reduced due to excessive information and the intrusion of data sources into our lives. Could it be that we will reach a time when it is quicker to discover something from scratch than from facts we can sort out from a library or the web?
